global-economics-0bc1fae315.headline: Origin raises $20 million from Accel, Zacua to scale construction robotics in the US, Europe
global-economics-0bc1fae315.fulltext:
Origin, a deeptech startup building autonomous robots for interior construction, has raised $20 million in a round led by Accel and Zacua Ventures as it emerges from stealth, with plans to build 150 robots by the end of next year. Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures, Z21, ISAI and Imad Ventures also invested, as did some of Origin’s customers. Accel’s India fund is the only Indian entity on the startup's cap table.
The raise is an early bet on physical artificial intelligence (AI) in one of the least automated industries. However, venture funds are increasingly parking money in the sector, with robotics in construction attracting $1.3 billion in funding until Q3 2025, compared to $612 million in all of 2024, according to Pitchbook data.
Origin’s pitch to its customers—large housing contractors in the US and Europe such as D.R. Horton and Lennar Corp.—centres on margin expansion amid high labour costs and worker shortages. These pressures have been compounded by tighter immigration curbs on white-collar and blue-collar workers in both regions.
"The cost of hiring skilled contractors in the US is very high. For a US contractor with a crew of five people, they pay $50,000 a month. Replacing them with a robot from us saves them 20% of the cost from day one," Yogesh Ghaturle, co-founder and chief executive of Origin, said in an interview with Mint.
Origin plans to have autonomous robots that can work on the entire interior construction of a home including things such as installation of heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, plumbing, dry wall painting. Currently however, the startup's flagship robot, the OG-1, is capable of completing wall-finishing. This includes sanding, applying primer paint, final painting.
Founded in January 2025 by Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, Origin rolled out its initial pilots and deployments in October 2025 and currently has six robots operational across the US and European markets.
The startup is currently focused on three priorities: scaling its painting operations with existing clients while finishing contracted projects and starting new pilots; stepping up manufacturing capacity; and building deployment teams across both markets. “We're planning to have built 150 robots by the end of next year,” Ghaturle said.
According to a Zacua Ventures report on construction robotics published in March, “Investors are paying up for autonomy in proven layout, piling and scanning workflows, while treating interior, MEP and façade robots as earlier-stage, higher-risk bets.”
Robots as a service
Origin's clients do not buy its robots outright; the startup operates on a subscription-based robots-as-a-service model instead, which Ghaturle described as “outcome as a service.” Its customers pay between $25,000 and $40,000 a month for access to the robots.
While Ghaturle declined to disclose the number of contracts Origin has signed, he said current deals average $2-2.5 million. “Our average contract value will be more like $5-$10 million as we sign more contracts,” he added.
A launch for Indian construction companies remains a few years away.
Building IP
Ghaturle describes Origin as a full-stack physical AI company, with intellectual property in hardware, software and AI. The robot is a modular, three-wheeled platform that is just 600-700mm wide and can work at heights up to 14 feet. It runs off-the-shelf power tools. “If you want to unlock a new tool on the platform, all you have to do is change the tool system and the end effector and a new use case will get unlocked on the platform,” he said.
On the software side, Origin is building what it calls construction action models — a class of robotics models for the industry. These help robots identify objects, navigate cluttered sites, avoid obstacles and work on ceilings.
Origin draws on three data sources: real-world data its deployed robots collect on job sites; photorealistic simulation and synthetic data, where it can randomize environments; and data from a lab where the team builds, breaks and rebuilds scenarios. Synthetic and lab data came first, but site data is now scaling the fastest.

Replacing them with a robot from us saves them 20% of the cost from day one," Yogesh Ghaturle, co-founder and chief executive of Origin, said in an interview with Mint.
Origin plans to have autonomous robots that can work on the entire interior construction of a home including things such as installation of heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, plumbing, dry wall painting. Currently however, the startup's flagship robot, the OG-1, is capable of completing wall-finishing. This includes sanding, applying primer paint, final painting.
Founded in January 2025 by Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, Origin rolled out its initial pilots and deployments in October 2025 and currently has six robots operational across the US and European markets.
The startup is currently focused on three priorities: scaling its painting operations with existing clients while finishing contracted projects and starting new pilots; stepping up manufacturing capacity; and building deployment teams across both markets. “We're planning to have built 150 robots by the end of next year,” Ghaturle said.
According to a Zacua Ventures report on construction robotics published in March, “Investors are paying up for autonomy in proven layout, piling and scanning workflows, while treating interior, MEP and façade robots as earlier-stage, higher-risk bets.”
Robots as a service
Origin's clients do not buy its robots outright; the startup operates on a subscription-based robots-as-a-service model instead, which Ghaturle described as “outcome as a service.” Its customers pay between $25,000 and $40,000 a month for access to the robots.
While Ghaturle declined to disclose the number of contracts Origin has signed, he said current deals average $2-2.5 million. “Our average contract value will be more like $5-$10 million as we sign more contracts,” he added.
A launch for Indian construction companies remains a few years away.
Building IP
Ghaturle describes Origin as a full-stack physical AI company, with intellectual property in hardware, software and AI. The robot is a modular, three-wheeled platform that is just 600-700mm wide and can work at heights up to 14 feet. It runs off-the-shelf power tools. “If you want to unlock a new tool on the platform, all you have to do is change the tool system and the end effector and a new use case will get unlocked on the platform,” he said.
On the software side, Origin is building what it calls construction action models — a class of robotics models for the industry. These help robots identify objects, navigate cluttered sites, avoid obstacles and work on ceilings.
Origin draws on three data sources: real-world data its deployed robots collect on job sites; photorealistic simulation and synthetic data, where it can randomize environments; and data from a lab where the team builds, breaks and rebuilds scenarios. Synthetic and lab data came first, but site data is now scaling the fastest.

india-deep-tech-e72ecc0d8d.headline: Construction robotics startup Origin raises $20 Mn led by Accel, Zacua Ventures
india-deep-tech-e72ecc0d8d.fulltext:
Origin, a physical AI startup building robots for interior construction, has raised $20 million in total funding in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. The round also saw participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21, along with angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla.
The company will use the funds to expand its robot fleet, deploy its flagship robot OG-1 and conduct customer pilots in the US and Europe. It also plans to expand its robotics platform to additional interior construction tasks.
Founded in 2025 by Yogesh Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, Origin develops robots designed to automate interior construction work. Its flagship robot, OG-1, currently handles wall finishing tasks such as applying compound, sanding and priming walls.
The robot is designed to operate across commercial spaces, residential apartments, data centres, hotels and warehouses. The company said it deployed its first robots at construction sites in New York within 10 months of its founding.
Origin is preparing for pilots with customers in the US and Europe, including two large drywall finishing contractors in the US. It also plans to conduct pilots in Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia.
The startup's robots are powered by its Construction Action Model, a foundation model developed for construction workflows. The system combines task planning, autonomous navigation and tool control to help robots perform construction tasks and adapt to changing site conditions.
Origin plans to expand OG-1's capabilities to tasks such as taping, drywall installation, drilling and conduit installation. The company is targeting the deployment of 150 robots by the end of 2027.
The funding comes amid rising interest in construction robotics as companies look to address labour shortages and improve productivity. According to a survey published by the Associated General Contractors of America in September 2026, worker shortages delayed projects for 42% of surveyed US construction firms.
A report by Zacua Ventures, published with Hilti Ventures and 94 Ventures, said construction robotics startups attracted $1.36 billion in venture funding in the first three quarters of 2025, compared with $612 million during the whole of 2024.
Ghaturle previously founded Perpule, a cloud-based point-of-sale startup that Amazon acquired in 2021. Makkar leads autonomy at Origin and previously worked at AI company Eightfold AI, while Daga leads hardware and has worked at digital pathology startup Morphle Labs.
Origin is headquartered in San Francisco and is deploying robots across construction sites in the US and Europe.

world-2bc3b4bbb3.headline: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
world-2bc3b4bbb3.fulltext:
Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
- Published
Seven of 12 crew members are missing after a drone attack left a chemical tanker ablaze off Romania's coast on Thursday morning, naval authorities say.
The San Marino-flagged Wine Trader was 13 nautical miles (24km) east of the mouth of the River Danube at Sulina, when it reported blasts and a fire.
Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed that the Wine Trader and another chemical tanker in the area, the Yara J, had both been struck by drones - the Yara J on Wednesday.
The Wine Trader was empty of cargo at the time.
Moscow said two cargo ships with military cargo heading to Ukraine's Odesa port had been hit. It did not name the vessels.
Overnight, a swarm of Russian drones was detected not far from the scene, near Ukraine's Snake Island.
The west coast of the Black Sea has recently seen a spate of drone attacks.
On Tuesday, two merchant ships were struck by drones further south along the coast of Bulgaria, Romania's neighbour, and one of the vessels sank, leaving 11 crew members missing.
Bulgaria said it suspected Russia was behind that attack, summoning the country's envoy.
A search and rescue operation for the missing members of the Wine Trader continues, Romania's authorities have said. Two Black Hawk helicopters and two rescue boats have been deployed.
The Romanian interior ministry has released a video showing one of the helicopters hovering above the vessel.
The priority is now to reach the four crew members confirmed to be alive, while ensuring the safety of rescue teams with very high waves reported in the area.
The Wine Trader tanker, which was sailing from Tunisia to Romania, reported several explosions on board at about 07:00 (05:00 GMT).
Romanian media cited crews on nearby ships as saying the Wine Trader had been hit by two drones.
The leaders of Romania and Bulgaria are due to discuss shortly whether Article 4 of the Nato treaty should be invoked.
This allows any member of the military alliance to request consultations with its allies if it believes its territorial integrity or security is threatened.
The Romanian president said: "We want to have all the information about what happened, but there will be a response from the Romanian state."
Dan is due to meet Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte in Brussels alongside Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev to discuss growing security threats in the Black Sea region.
The Romanian president said discussions would focus on operational requirements, including additional equipment to protect shipping in the area.
Ukraine has directly blamed Russia for earlier attacks on civilian vessels in the western side of the Black Sea - a key route for Ukrainian exports and imports.
On Tuesday, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen spoke of the Black Sea becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable".
Russia's military has recently intensified its strikes on vessels in the area, as part of its war against Ukraine.
A fire broke out on the Comoros-flagged Yara J late on Wednesday after being struck by a drone, but its crew - who are all reportedly safe - were able to douse the flames themselves.
Last week, another two ships were struck off Bulgaria, and on the same day Ukraine hit an oil tanker in the Russian Black Sea port of Sochi.
Moscow says it is targeting ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports.
Kyiv and its European allies say merchant vessels carrying grain and other civilian cargo are being attacked.
Both Russia and Ukraine are major grain-exporting countries and Turkey has called on both countries to halt attacks in the Black Sea.
Moscow has repeatedly rejected calls by the US and Europe for a naval ceasefire in the Black Sea, blaming Ukraine for attacking Russian merchant ships in the area.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

world-a7837e6e1f.headline: Seven sailors missing after drones strike tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast
world-a7837e6e1f.fulltext:
Seven sailors are missing after drones struck two tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast, setting them ablaze and raising fresh security concerns on a vital shipping route used by Ukraine.
A Nato military source told Reuters the drones that had hit the Wine Trader and the Yara J came from Russia. “The drones that caused the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the source said.
Romania’s president, Nicușor Dan, described the situation in the Black Sea as serious. “Commercial ships are being attacked and sunk,” he wrote on X. “Seafarers killed, injured and missing very close to the shores of Romania and Bulgaria. This is unacceptable and it has to stop.”
His statement followed a meeting with Bulgaria’s prime minister, Rumen Radev, and Nato’s secretary-general, Mark Rutte, on Thursday, where they agreed “to strengthen our defences in the Black Sea”, Dan said.
Rutte said: “Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed.”
A Nato official said the issue would be discussed at a meeting of the North Atlantic Council next week.
The missing crew were from the Wine Trader, a San Marino-flagged tanker travelling from Tunisia to Romania. All crew on the Yara J, which was struck just inside Romanian waters late on Wednesday, were safe.
Similar incidents in recent weeks have raised fears that the zone is becoming another front in Russia’s war on Ukraine.
Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones, but declined to say whether Russia was responsible.
Romania shares a 614km (381-mile) border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube. The country has experienced frequent drone incursions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, including a daytime encroachment last November that led Nato to scramble fighter jets.
EU leaders were already concerned about drone strikes on merchant ships off the coast of Bulgaria. On Tuesday, drone strikes on two ships off the coast of Bulgaria prompted emergency rescue operations, with 11 crew member from the HS Dignity, a cargo ship sailing under a Guinea-Bissau flag, still missing.
On another ship, the Ukrainian-operated Chelsea 3 sailing under a Maltese flag, rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries. The crew reported that the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones.
“The results of this attack favour Russia. However, we don’t have any solid evidence that the drones are Russians,” Radev said after arriving in Brussels for an EU summit on Thursday.
At least 23 sailors have been reported missing or killed after attacks on commercial shipping near the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania in the past 10 days, according to Reuters.
Russia has stepped up its bombing campaign on Ukraine’s Black Sea infrastructure, forcing Kyiv to turn to Danube river ports and Black Sea routes off the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria to export its grain, sunflower oil and other products.
According to a draft summit declaration, EU leaders will say that attacks against civilian shipping, including “member state-flagged vessels, such as the recent attacks in Bulgaria’s and Romania’s exclusive economic zones in the Black Sea, are unacceptable and constitute a serious violation of international and maritime law”.

global-economics-a565d27bcd.headline: Akash Ambani says Jio carries 60% of India's data traffic ahead of IPO, eyes major chunk of $1.4 tn digital economy
global-economics-a565d27bcd.fulltext:
Written By Prabhakar JhaPublished15 Oct 2026, 04:54 PM IST
Reliance Jio Infocomm Chairman Akash Ambani on Thursday said the telecom operator carries more than 60% of India's data traffic, while its data prices per GB are among the lowest in the world.
Speaking at a press conference ahead of Jio Platforms' initial public offering (IPO), Akash said the company aimed to help establish India as a leading digital society. The company released its red herring prospectus (RHP) on Wednesday.
Akash said India's digital economy is expected to reach $1.4 trillion by FY31, adding that Jio Platforms expects to capture a significant share of the market.
Jio had 533.3 million customers as of June 30, 2026. At 285 million, it also possesses the largest 5G customer base outside China. In the first quarter of FY27, its monthly data consumption per customer averaged around 43.7 GB.
Quick answers to key questions
•5 QUESTIONS
1
What share of India's data traffic does Jio carry?⌵
Reliance Jio Chairman Akash Ambani said Jio carries more than 60% of India's data traffic. He also said Jio's data prices per GB are among the lowest in the world.
2
How large is India's digital economy expected to become by FY31?⌵
Akash Ambani said India's digital economy is expected to reach $1.4 trillion by FY31. Jio Platforms expects to capture a significant share of that market.
3
How does Jio plan to grow beyond telecom?⌵
Jio's next phase includes artificial intelligence, enterprise services and digital applications. The company is developing enterprise tools and partnerships to deepen customer engagement.
4
Why is Jio Platforms' IPO significant for investors?⌵
The listing gives investors a clearer way to value Jio separately from Reliance Industries' oil business. A key question is whether Jio can turn its subscriber base into higher earnings through AI and digital services.
5
What are the key risks to consider in the Jio Platforms IPO?⌵
The prospectus identifies risks including customer retention and average revenue per user, network or technology disruptions, and dependence on Reliance Jio Infocomm. It also warns that AI and machine-learning technologies may not deliver expected results.
Akash also said that the company reported EBITDA of ₹76,225 crore in FY26 and its EBITDA margin stood at 53.3 per cent in the first quarter of FY27. The company's compound annual growth rate between FY24 and FY26 stood at 17.8%.
He also outlined the company's strategy based around technology, digital connectivity and infrastructure. These will be complemented by mobility, home broadband, and enterprise and international services, Akash added.
Jio's end-to-end technology platform is central to its growth strategy, Ambani said. Its connectivity business serves 533.3 million customers, supported by a network of 3,60,537 towers and 26,800 MHz of spectrum.
Jio expects the telecom industry to add 340 million 4G and 5G customers between FY26 and FY31, creating opportunities to increase average revenue per user (ARPU), a key measure of revenue generated per customer.
Home broadband is another growth driver. Jio had 28.6 million fixed broadband customers in FY26 and accounted for 67.5% of the industry's net additions during the year.
Highlighting the transformation of the digital connectivity in India since Jio entry in 2016, he said the average download speed has increased from 2.5 Mbps to 68 Mbps.
He also said that the average 5G download speed of Jio was 198.9 Mbps -- twice that of competing operators. Since Jio's entry the data costs have declined sharply in the country and remained among the lowest globally.
Akash also said the company's goal was to help make India a leading digital society, with Jio serving as a partner in that transformation.
The proposed Jio Platforms IPO is expected to focus investor attention on the company's vast subscriber base, profit growth and its ability to turn increasing data usage into revenue from higher-value digital services.
Akash Ambani positioned Jio Platforms as a technology business rather than merely a mobile operator, saying it plans to sell its proprietary network software and equipment to telecom operators overseas. However, the company's operations remain largely concentrated in India.
Reliance Industries' telecom and digital services arm, Jio Platforms, will launch its initial public offering on October 21, according to its red herring prospectus. The listing would mark the market debut of India’s largest mobile operator by subscriber numbers.

Jio Platforms plans to introduce next-generation 6G connectivity through a software upgrade rather than building new physical infrastructure, managing director Akash Mukesh Ambani said on Thursday, according to ANI.
Speaking at the Jio Platforms IPO press conference, he stated that the telecom giant's existing network infrastructure and proprietary core technology stack stand prepared for future technological transitions.
“Jio’s first mission is to democratize technology to benefit Indians. 6G is on our horizon. What this really means is that we will do 6G as a software upgrade rather than a new infrastructure build-out,” Ambani said.

Akash Ambani said Jio plans to introduce 6G through a software upgrade rather than a new physical infrastructure build-out.
2

Ambani said Jio’s existing network infrastructure and proprietary core technology stack are prepared for future technology transitions.
3
What existing network assets does Jio say support its 6G readiness?⌵
Jio has more than 360,000 towers, over 1 million route kilometres of fibre and what Ambani described as the industry’s largest spectrum bank.
4
When is Jio’s 6G rollout expected to begin?⌵
Ambani said 6G is on Jio’s horizon, but the article does not give a specific rollout date.
He attributed this readiness to Jio's extensive network footprint, which includes more than 360,000 towers across India and over 1 million route kilometres of fibre. The company also has the industry’s largest spectrum bank, he said.
Jio Platforms, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries Limited (RIL), has set the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) at ₹1,065- ₹1,119 per equity share. The issue will open for subscription on October 21 and close on October 23.
The company plans to issue up to 27 crore fresh equity shares of face value ₹10 each. The bidding for anchor investors, typically large institutional investors who invest ahead of a public offering, will take place on October 19.
The shares are slated to make their stock market debut on 28 October and are proposed to be listed on both BSE and NSE, according to the draft papers.
As per the news report, Ambani also highlighted Jio's financial performance, saying its revenue grew from ₹1.09 lakh crore to over ₹1.46 lakh crore in the past three years, registering a compound annual growth rate of 15.8%.
The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBIDTA) crossed ₹76,000 crore, while its margins stood at 53.3% in the first quarter of the financial year, he added.
“The basis of our EBITDA and our EBITDA growth has been us powering 60% of India's digital traffic. Today, Jio carries over 60% of India's data traffic,” Ambani stated, adding that 30% of revenue converts directly into free cash flow.
Jio Platforms has a subscriber base of 53 crore users and carries over 60% of India’s digital data traffic, Ambani noted. Customer data consumption averages 43.7 GB per month, while download speeds are nearly 200 Mbps, he added.
In the mobility segment, Jio is targeting a potential market of 340 million users, comprising 100 million first-time mobile users and 240 million subscribers who could migrate from legacy 2G networks.
Meanwhile in home broadband, the company aims to expand its reach from 30 million to 100 million households. To bypass right-of-way hurdles associated with physical fibre, the company developed an in-house wireless broadband solution operating on unlicensed bands, which accounts for 40% of its new additions.
Ambani also underscored plans to take Jio’s internally developed intellectual property abroad, backed by 7,220 patents filed by its engineering team.
“What we think is the end-to-end technology stack that we've created, deployed, and operate gives us the ability to partner with telecom partners across the world and really do this in a CAPEX-light manner,” Ambani said.

global-economics-e4c78caf6b.headline: Mutual funds suspend bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festival season
global-economics-e4c78caf6b.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
global-economics-e4c78caf6b.fulltext:
Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises.
The notices from the fund houses, including Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund, did not cite a reason for the move. There is no restriction on redemptions from these funds.
SEBI nudge preceded suspension
The decision was taken following a nudge from the Securities and Exchange Board of India, according to a mutual fund executive familiar with the discussions. Two bullion industry officials confirmed the halt had followed discussions with the market regulator.
The sources declined to be identified as they are not permitted to comment on discussions with the regulator.
A spokesperson for SEBI did not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours.
Rupee pressure and gold demand
The Indian rupee has been under pressure this year due to a surge in global oil prices, which have inflated the country’s import bill, and heavy selling by foreign investors in Indian equities. Strong demand for gold has further weighed on the currency, prompting the government to raise import duties on gold and silver earlier this year.
India, the world’s largest consumer of silver and second-largest consumer of gold, relies on imports to meet most of its demand, a dependence that can sometimes widen its trade deficit.
Gold imports fell to $1.8 billion in September, from $2.3 billion in August. However, Indians will celebrate Dussehra in October and Diwali in early November, when buying gold is considered auspicious.
Festival-season demand raises concerns
Inflows into gold and silver ETFs surged during last year’s festival season as investors turned to precious metals amid lackluster stock market returns.
The move is surprising, as gold and silver imports have fallen sharply over the past two months from a year earlier and have not contributed to the trade deficit, said a dealer at a private bank that supplies bullion to ETFs.
“It looks more like a precautionary measure to avoid a surge in imports in October,” the dealer said.

india-263ddb6f5c.headline: India’s September merchandise exports jump 23% as trade deficit narrows, US shipments rise 11%
india-263ddb6f5c.fulltext:
India's merchandise exports rose 23.04 per cent year-on-year to $44.40 billion in September 2026, up from $36.08 billion a year earlier, according to data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Thursday.The merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion from $33 billion in September last year, even as imports increased to $74.61 billion from $69.08 billion, the data showed.India's overall exports, including merchandise and services, grew 10.99 per cent to an estimated $80.75 billion in September, compared with $72.76 billion a year earlier.Overall imports rose to $94.05 billion from $86.93 billion, while the combined trade deficit narrowed to $13.30 billion from $14.17 billion, according to the ministry.
Electronics, engineering goods drive export growth
Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said merchandise shipments were driving the growth in exports."If you look at merchandise exports in September, they are at $44.40 billion, which is 23.04 per cent higher than last September," he said during a press briefing, according to news agency ANI.Higher shipments of electronic goods, petroleum products, engineering goods, chemicals and agricultural products supported the increase.Agrawal also said export growth had accelerated in the second quarter of the current financial year. Overall exports grew 15.84% in July-September, compared with 11.84 per cent in the first quarter, he said.According to the ministry's presentation, India's overall exports reached an estimated $242.6 billion in the second quarter, compared with $233.6 billion in April-June. The July-September figure was the highest ever recorded for the second quarter.
Imports rise as merchandise trade gap narrows
Merchandise imports increased to $74.61 billion in September from $70.67 billion in August, while exports rose from $43.81 billion to $44.40 billion over the same period, according to government data.The merchandise trade deficit stood at $30.21 billion, marginally below economists' expectations of $30.4 billion in a Reuters poll. However, it was higher than the $26.86 billion deficit recorded in August.Global energy prices remain a factor in India's import bill. Brent crude futures have stayed above $100 a barrel amid the Iran war, while attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have increased.Iran has said it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.
India looks to expand export markets
India is seeking to diversify its export markets through trade agreements with key partners. A trade deal with New Zealand is set to take effect next week, while India's trade pact with Britain is already in force. A broader agreement with the European Union is moving towards implementation.The United States remained India's largest merchandise export destination in the first half of the current financial year, despite tariff-related disruptions.India's merchandise exports to the US rose 11.1 per cent to $50.81 billion during April-September 2026, compared with $45.73 billion a year earlier.Imports from the US increased 26 per cent to $32.33 billion from $25.66 billion, according to data presented by the commerce ministry.India's merchandise trade surplus with the US narrowed to $18.48 billion from $20.07 billion in the corresponding period last year.Agrawal said negotiations for the proposed India-US trade agreement were progressing in the right direction, with both sides working towards concluding the deal at the earliest."The negotiations are in the right direction. New Delhi, Oct 15 (PTI) Healthy growth in shipments of petroleum products, electronic goods and chemicals helped India’s merchandise exports rise 23.04 per cent in September, while the trade deficit narrowed to USD 30.21 billion year-on-year due to a dip in imports of precious metals.
However, when compared to August, the deficit during the month under review widened from USD 26.86 billion. In September last year, it was USD 33 billion.
The country’s exports rose to USD 44.4 billion from USD 36.08 billion in September 2025, government data released on Thursday said.
Imports rose by 8 per cent year-on-year to USD 74.61 billion in September.
Gold and silver imports declined by 81.27 per cent and 49.11 per cent, respectively, to USD 1.8 billion and 665 million during the month. Inbound shipments of crude oil, on the other hand, rose by 30.76 per cent to USD 18.34 billion.
Brent crude oil prices have been hovering over USD 100 per barrel during the last few weeks.
Cumulatively, during April-September this fiscal, exports jumped 18.51 per cent to USD 259.89 billion, and imports climbed 16.31 per cent to USD 437.53 billion. The deficit during the first half of 2026-27 widened to USD 177.64 billion as compared to USD 156.88 billion during April-September 2025-26.
Exports are maintaining their growth trend, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said in a press briefing on trade data.
He expressed the hope that if the trend continued, the country’s merchandise exports would cross USD 500 billion. They were at USD 442 billion in 2025-26.
Exports of petroleum products, electronic goods and chemicals grew by 31.9 per cent (USD 6.2 billion), 70.44 per cent (USD 5.3 billion) and 24.21 per cent (USD 3 billion) respectively, during the month.
High crude oil prices amid the West Asia crisis have helped India earn better realisations from petroleum product exports.
As per government estimates, services exports stood at USD 36.35 billion in September, and imports were at USD 19.44 billion.
On services exports, the secretary said the rise in oil prices due to the West Asia crisis has impacted the exports in areas, including travel and tourism.

deep-tech-5150d9738e.fulltext:
[Text below is The Guardian's report of the same story — the original outlet blocks automated reading. The link still points to the original.]
Seven sailors are missing after drones struck two tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast, setting them ablaze and raising fresh security concerns on a vital shipping route used by Ukraine.
A Nato military source told Reuters the drones that had hit the Wine Trader and the Yara J came from Russia. “The drones that caused the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the source said.
Romania’s president, Nicușor Dan, described the situation in the Black Sea as serious. “Commercial ships are being attacked and sunk,” he wrote on X. “Seafarers killed, injured and missing very close to the shores of Romania and Bulgaria. This is unacceptable and it has to stop.”
His statement followed a meeting with Bulgaria’s prime minister, Rumen Radev, and Nato’s secretary-general, Mark Rutte, on Thursday, where they agreed “to strengthen our defences in the Black Sea”, Dan said.
Rutte said: “Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed.”
A Nato official said the issue would be discussed at a meeting of the North Atlantic Council next week.
The missing crew were from the Wine Trader, a San Marino-flagged tanker travelling from Tunisia to Romania. All crew on the Yara J, which was struck just inside Romanian waters late on Wednesday, were safe.
Similar incidents in recent weeks have raised fears that the zone is becoming another front in Russia’s war on Ukraine.
Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones, but declined to say whether Russia was responsible.
Romania shares a 614km (381-mile) border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube. The country has experienced frequent drone incursions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, including a daytime encroachment last November that led Nato to scramble fighter jets.
EU leaders were already concerned about drone strikes on merchant ships off the coast of Bulgaria. On Tuesday, drone strikes on two ships off the coast of Bulgaria prompted emergency rescue operations, with 11 crew member from the HS Dignity, a cargo ship sailing under a Guinea-Bissau flag, still missing.
On another ship, the Ukrainian-operated Chelsea 3 sailing under a Maltese flag, rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries. The crew reported that the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones.
“The results of this attack favour Russia. However, we don’t have any solid evidence that the drones are Russians,” Radev said after arriving in Brussels for an EU summit on Thursday.
At least 23 sailors have been reported missing or killed after attacks on commercial shipping near the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania in the past 10 days, according to Reuters.
Russia has stepped up its bombing campaign on Ukraine’s Black Sea infrastructure, forcing Kyiv to turn to Danube river ports and Black Sea routes off the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria to export its grain, sunflower oil and other products.
According to a draft summit declaration, EU leaders will say that attacks against civilian shipping, including “member state-flagged vessels, such as the recent attacks in Bulgaria’s and Romania’s exclusive economic zones in the Black Sea, are unacceptable and constitute a serious violation of international and maritime law”.

Cosmochute raises $1.5 mn pre-seed funding led by Accel, Prosus Ventures
The space robotics startup will use the funding to develop its modular lunar mobility platform and expand its engineering capabilities.
Cosmochute, a space robotics startup, has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Accel and Prosus Ventures through the Atoms X programme. IIMA Ventures’ deeptech and aerospace acceleration fund, Operators Studio, and Chinmayi Muthyala also participated in the round.
Cosmochute is building robotics and infrastructure for the emerging lunar economy. LEAP combines a rover and trailer with standardised payload bays to transport and deploy equipment on the Moon. The company aims to reduce the cost and complexity of lunar missions by limiting the need for bespoke engineering for individual payloads.
“Space 1.0 was ISRO proving India could reach orbit. Space 2.0 made orbit commercial: cheaper, more frequent, and open to private capital,” said Janhavi Gore, co-founder of Cosmochute.
“With sustainable access now secured, we believe it’s the moment for Space 3.0 — what happens after you make the in-space economy operable and extend it to the surface of the Moon,” she added.
The startup is setting up its lunar laboratories at IIMA Ventures’ incubation facility and is guided by Mylswamy Annadurai, former programme director of Chandrayaan-1.
It plans to build capabilities across lunar mobility and space robotics, targeting future commercial and scientific missions to the Moon.
“Cosmochute builds on our conviction that the infrastructure for a lunar economy can be both technically feasible and commercially viable. Their first-principles thinking, technical expertise, and systems approach is exactly what we look for,” said Pratik Agarwal, partner at Accel.

Space robotics startup Cosmochute has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Accel and Prosus Ventures through the Atoms X programme.
The round also saw participation from IIMA Ventures’ Deeptech and Aerospace Acceleration Fund, Operators Studio and Chinmayi Muthyala.
The startup plans to use the funding to develop its lunar mobility platform, expand its engineering team and advance its commercial plans.
Atoms X is an early-stage investment programme that supports startups developing technologies in areas including space, climate and healthcare. Backed by Accel and Prosus, the programme provides funding, mentorship and access to industry networks.
What does Cosmochute do?
Founded by Janhavi Gore, Amit Chowdhary and Dhruv Alok Sangal, Ahmedabad-based Cosmochute is developing robotics and transportation infrastructure to support commercial and scientific activities on the Moon.
Its first programme, LEAP, is a modular lunar mobility platform designed to transport and deploy equipment and payloads on the lunar surface.
The platform combines a rover and trailer with standardised payload bays, allowing different types of equipment to be accommodated within a common transportation system.
Cosmochute aims to address the cost and complexity of lunar missions, where transporting and deploying equipment can require engineering tailored to individual payloads.
By standardising parts of the transportation and deployment process, the company hopes to reduce the need for mission-specific engineering and make lunar operations more repeatable.
“Space 1.0 was ISRO proving India could reach orbit. Space 2.0 made orbit commercial: cheaper, more frequent, and open to private capital,” said Janhavi Gore, co-founder of Cosmochute.
“With sustainable access now secured, we believe it’s the moment for Space 3.0, what happens after you make the in-space economy operable and extend it to the surface of the Moon,” she added.
Expanding lunar robotics capabilities
Cosmochute is setting up lunar laboratories at IIMA Ventures’ incubation facility, according to reports of the funding announcement.
The startup's scientific team includes Mylswamy Annadurai, former programme director of India's Chandrayaan-1 mission, who is listed as its chief scientist.
Beyond LEAP, Cosmochute plans to develop broader capabilities in lunar mobility and space robotics, with potential applications in other space operations and on Earth.
Its longer-term objective is to build infrastructure that could support future commercial and scientific missions to the Moon.
“Cosmochute builds on our conviction that the infrastructure for a lunar economy can be both technically feasible and commercially viable. Their first-principles thinking, technical expertise, and systems approach is exactly what we look for,” said Pratik Agarwal, partner at Accel.
Dhruv Gupta, an investor at Prosus, said At Prosus Ventures, we actively explore frontier technologies spanning specialised engineering, deep technology and future-economy infrastructure, supporting founders as they build ambitious companies on their terms.
“We are incredibly excited to back Cosmochute and welcome them to Atoms X - the platform for leaptech pioneers from India,” Gupta said.
